title: A “Molecular Water Pipe”: A Giant Tubular Cluster {Dy72} Exhibits Fast Proton Transport and Slow Magnetic Relaxation

material_class.structural_family: Porous, saddle-like tubular lanthanide oxo/hydroxo coordination cluster

synthesis.procedure: Dy(NO3)3·5H2O, N-methyldiethanolamine, triethylamine, and methanol were mixed in a sealed glass vial and heated at 130 °C under autogenous pressure for five days. The resulting colorless spindle crystals were isolated and washed with anhydrous methanol.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Sealed glass vial; heating under autogenous pressure
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Colorless spindle crystals were isolated and washed with anhydrous methanol.

properties.summary: PCC-72 shows magnetic anisotropy and frequency-dependent out-of-phase ac susceptibility at zero applied dc field, consistent with slow magnetic relaxation. Proton conduction is also reported but is outside the requested magnetic/optical property categories.

measurements.name: χT
measurements.conditions: Room temperature; dc susceptibility measured under 1000 Oe

measurements.name: Estimated relaxation barrier U/kB
measurements.conditions: Estimated from ac susceptibility at zero dc field, assuming one Debye-type relaxation process

measurements.name: Characteristic relaxation time τ0
measurements.conditions: Estimated from ac susceptibility at zero dc field

measurements.name: Estimated relaxation time τ
measurements.conditions: 2 K; calculated using the Arrhenius law

source_locations.location: Supporting Experiment Section, synthesis of PCC-72

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The discrete Dy72 core is a saddle-like tube assembled from Dy3 hydroxo triangles, Dy4 oxo tetrahedra, and Dy5 hydroxo square-pyramids linked by shared vertices, edges, or faces. A central 24-Dy square-wheel belt is flanked by two 24-Dy wheel-like units, producing a hydrophilic tubular opening.
